**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

- **Preferred position met.** There is no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding Redwood. § 12.3 goes further and affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service, engage any supplier, and conduct business in any field or territory, and has Silverline acknowledge that we made no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. § 2.1 confirms no minimum or purchase commitment.
- **Restrictions on us are benign.** § 13.4 contains only standard acceptable-use limits (no reverse engineering, no interference with the Services, no unlawful use), with law-mandated and security-testing carve-outs — not competitive restraints.
- **Noted, not flagged here.** § 2.2 ("Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term") is a sole-source commitment that directly contradicts § 12.3. It functions as an exclusivity term rather than a non-compete, so it is handled under the exclusivity rule to avoid double-flagging the same commercial term. Worth confirming that the exclusivity review deletes it, since leaving both provisions in place creates an internal conflict.
